verdicts.trueWording: naturally divide the city into wards (neighborhoods defined by specific features)
verdicts.note: archive.org _djvu.txt OCR of the 2014 DMG fetched raw by curl; the string appears at OCR line 2576 in the Settlements > Size > City passage. Both limbs hold: the preceding sentence has the stages of a city's growth identified by the expansion of the walls beyond the central core, and it is those internal walls that divide the city into wards. Section attribution ch.1 Settlements > Size > City is consistent (the Purpose section begins p.15 per a second source).

verdicts.trueWording: "settlement" appears twice: selling treasure, and hirelings from a distant settlement
verdicts.note: Publisher PDF fetched raw by curl (3.1 MB), pdftotext -layout, 3.35 MB of text. Measured: grep -o -i settlement returns exactly 2 hits. Hit 1 is the treasure-selling clause; hit 2 is the hirelings passage. Zero hits for Race Relations, Ruler's Status, Notable Traits, Known for, Current Calamity, Metropolis, Forms of Government; no Settlements/Towns/Cities heading. Both limbs confirmed. No quote was supplied so this is graded SUBSTANCE, not VERBATIM.

verdicts.trueWording: four "settlement" hits, all spell text; no settlement section or tables
verdicts.note: Publisher PDF fetched raw by curl (6.0 MB), pdftotext -layout, 2.15 MB of text. Four occurrences of settlement, every one inside spell or item text (commune with nature's Locations of settlements bullet, a druid-magic exclusion, a castles-and-settlements clause, a materials clause). Zero hits for Notable Traits, Current Calamity, Race Relations, Metropolis, Town Encounters, Settlement Tracker; no Settlements heading. Both limbs confirmed; no quote supplied, so SUBSTANCE.

verdicts.trueWording: doesn't include an index of all of the random charts
verdicts.note: Live URL fetched raw with a browser user agent, HTML stripped locally. Quote appears verbatim in the second paragraph. The Random Table Index table then gives every figure the claim asserts: Race Relations 112, Ruler's Status 112, Notable Traits 112, Known For Its 112, Current Calamity 112, and Forms of Government 18 near the head of the index. Every limb supported.

verdicts.trueWording: is less about what settlements are like in the world
verdicts.note: Live URL fetched raw with a browser user agent, HTML stripped locally. The sentence reads that the Purpose section, beginning on page 15 of the DMG, is less about what settlements are like in the world than about how much the GM should invent and record about them. Both halves of the claim's contrast are present. Authorship confirmed by the page's rel=author link to /author/ian/.

verdicts.trueWording: The DMG divides settlements just by population
verdicts.note: Same raw fetch. Quote verbatim, and it sits under the 'Village' sub-heading as the claim's page field says. The function limb is supported by the next sentences: historians draw a distinction in nature between villages and towns whose population ranges overlap, villages being agricultural units and towns commercial units. Disputes polarity is right.

verdicts.trueWording: more of a bullet-point list of suggestions than a guide
verdicts.note: Live URL fetched raw with a browser user agent (2.1 MB of HTML), stripped locally. The quoted fragment is contiguous and verbatim; the full sentence continues 'to cooking up good ideas of your own'. The settlement limb is supported in the immediately preceding sentence, which names the toolbox's tables for dungeons and settlement creation. Complaint/disputes polarity is right.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'the Settlement Tracker among them' - the page never names a sheet 'Settlement Tracker'; it says only that the sheets cover settlements among key NPCs, Bastions, magic items and backstories
verdicts.trueWording: designed to help you keep track of important information
verdicts.note: Live URL fetched raw with a browser user agent, HTML stripped locally. Perkins' quoted words appear verbatim ('these sheets are designed to help you keep track of important information in your game'), attributed to an official livestream from October 1, by-lined Mollie Russell. grep for 'settlement tracker' over the raw HTML returns 0. Downstream fix is one word: write 'settlements among them' rather than naming the sheet. Note also the article calls the guide upcoming, so this is pre-release reporting.

verdicts.trueWording: All that took about 30 seconds to create using the tables
verdicts.note: Live Substack URL fetched raw with a browser user agent; the whole short post is in the HTML, not paywalled. Quote verbatim, continuing 'on pg. 112 (and the tavern name on 113)'. The demonstration is a single connected paragraph immediately above it, carrying page-112 slots visibly: harmony (Race Relations), a kind, just, and respected former war hero (Ruler's Status), sinister reputation (Notable Traits row 17), marauding monsters (Calamity row 8-9). Byline Maximilian Hart, dated Oct 27, 2022.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'the full row lists' - the reproduction's Notable Traits stops at row 19, omitting the DMG's row 20 (built atop ancient ruins), and its Ruler's Status ranges are malformed (17-18 and 18-20 overlap where the book has 19-20)
verdicts.note: Live URL fetched raw with a browser user agent, HTML stripped locally. The p.112 citation is verbatim as footnote 1 at the foot of the page, and all five named tables are reproduced with row lists. But the lists are not full: I cross-checked against the 2014 DMG OCR, where Notable Traits is a d20 with 20 rows ending 'Built atop ancient ruins', and Ruler's Status ends 19-20 Religious leader. The supplied low-confidence caveat is also confirmed on the page - it additionally prints Community Sizes (thorp/hamlet bands), Overall Alignment and a d100 Government table, none of which are 5e settlement tables.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'opening on the city's physical situation' - the description's first paragraph is an adventure hook (would-be heroes drawn by promises of adventure); the river placement is the second paragraph
verdicts.trueWording: The city stands on the eastern banks of the Selintan River.
verdicts.note: roll20.net licensed compendium page fetched raw with a browser user agent; the body text is present in the HTML despite the purchase banner. Quote verbatim. The present-tense limb holds across the section (stands, flows, remains, is ruled, winds), with past tense reserved for the historical clause. Only the 'opening' limb misses by one paragraph, so the safe downstream wording is 'turns to the city's physical situation in its second paragraph'.

verdicts.trueWording: proclaimed itself free and independent seventy-eight years ago

verdicts.trueWording: made up of sixteen coequal rulers
verdicts.note: Same raw roll20 fetch. Quote verbatim and it does sit under the 'City Government' heading as the page field says: the council is the Directing Oligarchy and its membership count is spelled in words, not given as a numeral.

verdicts.trueWording: a standing garrison of some eight hundred
verdicts.note: Same raw roll20 fetch. Quote verbatim under the 'City Watch' heading; the sentence continues into linked creature names (Guards and Veteran Warriors). The garrison size is spelled in words. Both limbs hold.

verdicts.trueWording: A 30-foot-high stone wall winds like a snake around the city.
verdicts.note: Same raw roll20 fetch. Quote verbatim as the first sentence under 'City Walls'. It is running prose, not a stat line, and the measurement is a numeral - and the same section keeps that habit (secret compartments at 300-foot intervals, a 30-foot-tall ladder, a sentry every 300 feet), so the contrast with the spelled-out counts in 973-975 is a real and consistent house rule: counts of people and years in words, physical measurements in numerals.
